html:
The military ruler of Uganda from 1971 to 1979, one of the most brutal dictators of the 20th century. He joined the British colonial army, the King's African Rifles, and rose to command Uganda's army after independence.

In January 1971 he overthrew President Milton Obote in a coup. At first many welcomed him, but his rule turned to terror. Soldiers and secret police killed opponents, ethnic groups seen as loyal to Obote, and anyone suspected of disloyalty. Estimates of the dead run from 100,000 to 500,000.

  • In 1972 he ordered the expulsion of Uganda's Asians, about 80,000 people, and handed their businesses to his supporters. The economy collapsed.
  • In 1976 Israeli commandos freed hostages he had let hijackers hold at Entebbe airport, in Operation Entebbe.
  • In 1978 he invaded Tanzania. Nyerere's army and Ugandan exiles struck back and took Kampala in April 1979.

He fled to Libya and then Saudi Arabia, where he lived until his death in 2003, never tried for his crimes.
